thread_title: S. oreophila var. ornata purple throat 'orange tinge'
breadcrumb: S. oreophila var. ornata purple throat 'orange tinge'

posts.body_html:
Here's a really interesting S. oreophila clone that has heavy veins, a purple (ish) throat, and most imporantly, gets an incredible orange tinge once the traps age! Right now, the plant hasn't yet fully colored up, but it's looking pretty nice and just starting to get some interesting colors.

In the past few year, as the traps age, they all turned a slight orange color, so I'm thinking this is likely a genetic trait. Hopefully it will show its true colors in the next month or so, but for now, there's still a pretty nice show. Photos taken 6/18/18:


I guess these are light activated anthocyanins? Some of the orangy color is just starting to show up on the lids, but this ain't nuthin compared to later on:











To be continued....if it fully colors up as expected

posts.body_html: gorgeous plant. I've seen in Barry Rice's vids on oreo that some of the plants in the wild indeed have copper-colored lids, quite strong coloration too, but never as chocolatey as flava. I believe it's not too uncommon actually, but very few of those sorts of clones are in cultivation, especially on v. ornata plants. Is this a creation of yours, Mike?
